name: Washington Ecology Sewage Spills list (RCW 90.48.636 public website)
waters_covered: statewide; spills reported under individual water quality permits
access_detail: The page embeds an ArcGIS Experience ('Sewage spill table only', item 4fb5f533aabb41ce9e5bd8aa59284ab6) whose table reads the public hosted layer https://gis.ecology.wa.gov/hosting/rest/services/Hosted/survey123_48de962d0dea40eb9485805510a40b84_results/FeatureServer/0 (Query, Extract; 72 reports from 2026-06-15 on 2026-11-04). The portal, item and layer answered HTTP 200 to the project user agent on 2026-11-04; the firewall refusal of 2026-11-03 was with another client. Every point on the layer is 0,0.
cadence: 'After we receive the report from the facility, our goal is to publish the information within five working days.' Final information added after the spill concludes.
history: Every report since the site began (2026-06-15) stays on the layer.
license: Page disclaimer: 'This information is provided as it has been reported. It has not been independently verified by Ecology. The information is provided for educational, informational, and research purposes.'
status_reason: The statewide dated feed Washington's law requires, read by pipeline/ingest/wa_ecology_spills.py.
notes: Excludes private backups, illegal dumping and other spills. Ecology reports roughly 300 sewage spills a year (search).

name: RCW 90.48.636 Sewage spills - Website - Notices (2025 c 315, Sewage Spill Right to Know)
status_reason: State duty to publish each permitted facility's reported sewage spill on a public website.
notes: (1) 'By July 1, 2026, the department must develop and publish a public-facing website that includes, but is not limited to, notices of the locations where sewage spills occur that are reported to the department under individual water quality permits for discharges that contain sewage. The department must post on the website notice of the reported sewage spill.' Content (a)-(g): estimated volume or rate and final volume; level of treatment; date and time initiated; location; once known the time ceased; 'The geographic area potentially impacted'; steps to contain. (2) update with final information 'Within a reasonable amount of time following the conclusion'. (3) limited-English-proficiency design. No posting deadline in the statute. RCW 90.48.632(2) defines sewage spill as 'the intentional or accidental discharge of untreated or undertreated wastewater that does not meet permit requirements', including combined sewers.
